blocks.text: Between June 2026 and October 2026, detached houses: listings fell from 164 in June to 158 in October (−3.7%), and it took 75.4% of the city’s 167 sales over the period; condos and townhomes: listings fell from 109 in June to 105 in October (−3.7%), and it took 41.5% of the city’s 193 sales over the period.

The monthly write-ups singled out Cloverdale for detached houses in June, October (a sellers’ best bet); detached houses in July, August, September (a buyers’ best bet); condos and townhomes in August (a sellers’ best bet); condos and townhomes in June, July, September, October (a buyers’ best bet).

blocks.text: Condo buildings in Cloverdale

The marketing name "Compass" covers two different forms in Clayton: an apartment-condo phase at 18755 68 Avenue (and 6815 188 Street) described as condos in its source, and townhouse units at 18777 68A Avenue that current listings classify as Row / Townhouse.
St. Andrews at Northview — 16421 64 Avenue (eight addresses: 16421, 16433, 16447, 16455, 16469, 16477, 16483 and 16499 64 Avenue)

A gated condo community by Rempel Development Group at 64 Avenue & 164 Street, beside Northview Golf Course: the building directory records Strata Plan BCS2562, 3 levels, 219 units across eight three-storey buildings, built 2009, with homes of 1,264–1,866 sq ft and an 8,000+ sq ft club with outdoor pool, fitness centre, media room, library and guest suites. Current listings classify units as Apartment/Condo and record freehold strata title. Year note: individual listings for the 16469/16477 addresses state 2007/2008 build years against the directory's 2009 for 16421. Published restrictions (directory): 1 cat or 1 dog allowed; "Rentals Allowed w/Restrictions" — the rental half of that line is void in law since November 24, 2022.
Waterstone — 6420 / 6440 194 Street (Clayton)

An apartment-condo complex in Clayton: current listings record sub-type Apartment/Condo, built 2010, freehold strata, built around a 15,000 sq ft clubhouse with indoor 60-foot pool, whirlpool, steam room, sauna, fitness centre and guest suite. A building-directory listing header records a 274-unit development, wood frame — that figure is the directory's development total for the complex, not a per-address count. Published pet restrictions: a current listing header records "Pets Allowed".
Calera — 18818 68 Avenue (Clayton)

An apartment-condo building in Clayton Village: the building directory records 153 units and a 2010 build, with bike room, club house, exercise centre, in-suite laundry, recreation centre and storage; current listings record sub-type Apartment/Condo, freehold strata, built 2010, with one listing recording "Cats OK" for that unit. Published restrictions (directory): "Pets allowed w/rest., rentals allwd w/restrctns" — the rental half is void since November 24, 2022.
Compass (apartment phase) — 18755 68 Avenue (and 6815 188 Street), Clayton

A condo phase described in its source as two 4-level wood-frame buildings, built 2008, with 1-bedroom, 1-bedroom-plus-den and 2-bedroom condos and two pets allowed; the same source gives 104 homes for the whole Compass complex, which also includes the townhouse units below. The directory line "Rentals allowed with restrictions" is void since November 24, 2022.
Where the condos are and what to know

items.t: MLS® areas don’t match City boundaries: in the SnapStats data, "Cloverdale" is its own Fraser Valley board community — separate from the Surrey community — made up of three sub-areas: Clayton, Cloverdale and Serpentine.
The board does not publish sub-area medians — community medians only, labelled as such.

The apartment buildings here sit in two pockets — Clayton Heights around 68 Avenue / 188–194 Street (Calera, Compass, Waterstone), and the Cloverdale town-centre / Northview edge at 64 Avenue & 164 Street (St. Andrews at Northview). The rest of the attached pool is predominantly townhouse complexes.

Town Centre plan: the City is updating the Cloverdale Town Centre Plan; the plan area is at the intersection of Highway 10 and Highway 15 (Pacific Highway), and on July 22, 2024 Council expanded the plan boundary northward — bounded by 60th Avenue (south), 175 and 175A Street (west), 64 Avenue (north) and 180 Street (east), plus one lot at 18120 56 Ave, covering roughly 80.8 hectares and 145 properties. The Cloverdale Fairgrounds are a Special Study Area outside the Town Centre Plan's own scope.

Transit: no SkyTrain station is inside Cloverdale today. The City states three new stations are planned for Cloverdale under the approved expansion, and TransLink states the Surrey-Langley SkyTrain is a 16-kilometre Expo Line extension along Fraser Highway from King George Station to 203 Street in Langley City, with an anticipated in-service date of 2029.
"Cloverdale" means three different geographies. The City community, the board community (Clayton + Cloverdale + Serpentine) and the Town Centre plan area are three different footprints.
Serpentine shows zero in the residential tables and still trades. A zero row is not an empty market.

Two of the biggest "condo" amenities packages are clubhouses, not towers. St. Andrews' 8,000+ sq ft Club and Waterstone's 15,000 sq ft clubhouse (indoor 60-foot pool) sit inside low-rise, gated, townhouse-scale communities — fee and amenity comparisons against a standard Clayton low-rise mislead without the clubhouse line.

Clayton was the community's fastest shelf in September 2026. Clayton's sales ratios (29% detached, 21% attached) led the Cloverdale set that month, ahead of the Cloverdale sub-area (13% / 17%) — a Clayton condo and a town-centre condo faced different shelves, on medians published only at community level.

The Fairgrounds are outside the Town Centre Plan. The Cloverdale Fairgrounds — home to the Cloverdale Rodeo, held there since 1945 — are designated a Special Study Area under a separate City study and are not within the Town Centre Plan's scope, so plan-area claims for fairgrounds-adjacent property need the separate study, not the plan.

blocks.text: Lots and land in Cloverdale
What trades here

items.t: Bare-land strata — the form, no Cloverdale instance known: A bare-land strata lot is strata tenure ON the lot itself: the buyer takes a strata lot, pays strata fees, is bound by the strata's bylaws, and is entitled to a Form B Information Certificate for the lot — it is not fee-simple ownership with a road association. Tenure is read lot by lot on title.

Lot character: there is no Cloverdale-wide lot-size table. What governs what a lot can become is the density rules: SSMUH unit counts by lot-size band, coach house / garden suite sizes of 35–75 m² (up to 120 m² on RA, R2, R2-O and R3 lots below maximum FAR), and the July 8, 2024 zone replacements (former RF-12 / RF-12C → R4 Small Lot Residential; RF-SD → R6 Semi-Detached).

ALR vs non-ALR split: The Cloverdale community includes ALR farm parcels on its lowland side; the ALC housing frame for those parcels is one principal residence at a maximum of 500 m² plus at most one additional residence of 90 m² (parcels ≤40 ha) or 186 m² (parcels >40 ha). Parcel-level ALR status governs; the farm ground itself is documented in
Clayton's 9: Sun @ 72; Clayton Walk; The Grove (Clayton — a DIFFERENT complex from Walnut Grove's condo The Grove); Creekside; Ixia; The Belmont; Balmoral; The Edge; Montana.
A lot inside the plan area carries plan upside and plan uncertainty until the update is adopted.

Market context, labelled as such: SnapStats covers Cloverdale as a community but has no land category (Detached vs "Condos & Townhomes" combined only), and land has no SnapStats category anywhere. Sub-area rows: Clayton detached 34 / 10 / 29%, Cloverdale detached 167 / 22 / 13%, Serpentine 0 / 0 / NA in both splits. No detached figure here is a land figure. (SnapStats FVR September 2026 report.)

items.t: Location as the City states it: Cloverdale is the third largest community in Surrey; its western border runs along 160 Street and connects with 48 Avenue, which is the southern border; Langley is to the east, and Guildford and Fleetwood are to the north, separated by 84 Avenue and 76 Avenue.

Character as the City states it: the historic centre of Surrey, settled in the mid to late 1800s, grown from a largely rural and agricultural community, named from Clover Valley, and developed along the railway into a railway and commercial hub; it has hosted the Cloverdale Rodeo at the Cloverdale Fairgrounds since 1945.
Serpentine — dual filing stated.

Town Centre plan area: at the intersection of Highway 10 and Highway 15 (Pacific Highway); the boundary was expanded northward July 22, 2024 — bounded by 60th Avenue (south), 175 and 175A Street (west), 64 Avenue (north) and 180 Street (east), plus one lot at 18120 56 Ave, roughly 80.8 hectares and 145 properties.
The Cloverdale Fairgrounds are designated a Special Study Area under a separate City study and are not within the scope of the Cloverdale Town Centre Plan.
Search names: "Cloverdale BC," "Cloverdale Surrey," "Clayton Heights."

ALR block (applies to Cloverdale's lowland ALR parcels): ALR residences cannot be stratified; subdivision within the ALR requires ALC approval; principal residence ≤500 m², a suite within the principal residence only, and one additional residence of 90 m² (parcels ≤40 ha) or 186 m² (parcels >40 ha).
Clayton moved faster than the rest of Cloverdale in September 2026 — and Serpentine recorded nothing residential at all. (SnapStats FVR September 2026 report.)

Three SkyTrain stations are planned for Cloverdale. The City states three new stations are planned under the approved expansion; TransLink states the Surrey-Langley SkyTrain is a 16-km Expo Line extension along Fraser Highway from King George Station to 203 Street in Langley City, anticipated in service 2029.
Clayton Community Centre is the community's combined arts/recreation/library building. Clayton Community Centre, 7155 187A Street, integrates arts, recreation and a library in Cloverdale.

The ground in Cloverdale

items.t: The lowland ALR edge: Serpentine's September 2026 residential rows are 0 / 0 in both splits because its trading is farm / agri-business product the residential table does not capture — a zero row is not an empty market.
Serviced vs unserviced ground: the urban core is serviced ground in its built form; the lowland farm edge is rural parcel ground whose servicing is a per-parcel question.

blocks.text: Where the acreages are and what to know

items.t: Amenity anchor: Clayton Community Centre, 7155 187A Street, is open and integrates arts, recreation and a library in Cloverdale.
City plan: The Cloverdale Town Centre Plan is being updated (boundary expanded July 22, 2024; Fairgrounds excluded as a Special Study Area).

If a strata purchase is made in Cloverdale (the townhome product here), the BC strata rules apply: Form B diligence; depreciation reports on a 5-year cycle for stratas with 5+ lots since July 1, 2024; minimum 10% CRF contribution since November 1, 2023; rental-restriction bylaws void since November 24, 2022; only 55+ age bylaws valid (SPA ss.123.1/123.2, May 1, 2023 exemptions). Charlton's developer sales additionally carry 5% GST (subject to the rebates above) and the REDMA requirements (disclosure statement, deposits in trust under s.18, 7-day rescission under s.21). Pad ground is not lot stock, land or acreage. Pad tenancy increases are percentages only (2026 = 2.3% + proportionate; 2027 = 2.2% + proportionate); no pad-rent dollar figure is stated.

faq.a: No — Cloverdale is one of the City of Surrey's seven communities, described by the City as its historic centre and its third largest community, with Langley to the east and Guildford and Fleetwood to the north. In board data it is also its own community, separate from the Surrey community, with three sub-areas: Clayton, Cloverdale and Serpentine.
The rest of the 194-listing attached pool (September 2026) is predominantly townhouse complexes.
faq.q: How many true apartment-condo buildings are there in Cloverdale?

faq.a: Both, under one name. The 18755 68 Avenue phase is described as condos; the 18777 68A Avenue units are classified Row / Townhouse in current listings.
faq.q: Compass — is it condos or townhouses?

faq.a: Yes — strata rental-restriction bylaws have been unenforceable since November 24, 2022 anywhere in BC, so the "rentals allowed w/restrictions" directory lines for St. Andrews, Calera and Compass no longer bind. Short-term rentals can still be restricted by bylaw, and Surrey separately requires an owner-host living at the property with a $358/year licence.
faq.q: Can I rent out a Cloverdale condo long-term?

faq.a: Clayton moved fastest in both splits (29% detached, 21% attached); Serpentine recorded no residential listings or sales. No sub-area median is published.
faq.q: How did Cloverdale sell in September 2026?

faq.a: Both, under one name. The 18755 68 Avenue phase is apartment condos; the 18777 68A Avenue units are Row / Townhouse in current listings.
faq.q: Compass — is it condos or townhouses?

faq.a: Long-term, yes under provincial law: strata rental-restriction bylaws have been void since Nov 24, 2022, whatever an older directory prints.
faq.q: Can I rent out my Cloverdale townhouse?

faq.a: No counted complex is published as age-restricted — check the registered bylaws on the Form B before assuming either way.
faq.q: Is there a 55+ townhouse in Cloverdale?

faq.a: Compass splits by address and form: only the 18777 68A Ave townhouse units count as townhouses; the 18755 68 Ave apartment phase is condos only.
faq.q: Are Clayton Rise, Compass, Charlton, Laredo, Sunberry Court, Bacara or Manhattan Skye acreage or bare-land strata?

faq.a: On urban ground: one secondary suite per dwelling unit (at most 40% of the principal unit, never inside a coach house or garden suite), a coach house or garden suite of 35–75 m² (up to 120 m² only on RA, R2, R2-O and R3 lots below maximum FAR), and 3–4 SSMUH units on most lots by size band, up to 6 near a frequent bus stop. On ALR ground the answer is the ALC's, not the City's: a suite only inside the principal residence, and any second dwelling is the size-capped additional residence.
